title: Dobsonian telescope
summary: give your mirror, get the telescope
description: A Newtonian on a plywood rocker box, from your mirror: the secondary for the field you choose, the spider, the focuser position, the altitude bearings on the real balance point (computed from the masses, then measured on the model), the rocker box and a cut sheet for the plywood.
process: Plywood cutting (saw, router or CNC), paper form tube, mirror cell assembly

difficulty.rationale: Closed-form centre of mass over 20+ bodies checked by measure, swept clearance, many coupled range formulas, structure changing by choice.

standards: Mike Lockwood, loptics.com: secondary sizing table and offset, 0.5 in field for general use (https://www.loptics.com/ATM/diagonals.html)

Stellafane ATM: Dobsonian OTA design (tube ID about 2 in over the mirror, spare in-travel 1/4 to 1/2 in, https://stellafane.org/tm/dob/ota/design.html), rocker box (sides about 1.2 tube OD, swing margin at least 2 in) and ground board
Reiner Vogel, rocker box notes: Teflon pads at 35 degrees, 1 cm2 of Teflon per kg (citing Kriege and Berry), http://www.reinervogel.net/Planung/5_Rocker_e.html
materials: Birch plywood 12 to 24 mm (rocker box, ground board, altitude bearings, mirror cell plate)
Paper concrete-form tube, rolled aluminium or glass-fibre tube
Focuser, eyepiece and finder of your choice
